title: Meta turns to a $35B equity raise, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom lining up as buyers
intro: The weekend and Monday were about paying for the build-out: Meta filed for roughly $35B of new stock and preferred shares with its own chip suppliers indicating interest, and SpaceX lined up about $40B of Apollo-managed lease financing for Nvidia GPUs. Tracked value recovered 1.0% between the Oct 23 and Oct 26 closes (Taiwan closed since Oct 22), with EDA, energy, compute and optics leading while packaging and Japanese equipment names lagged.
movers_note: Between the Oct 23 and Oct 26 closes (53 names with a new quote; Taiwan listings unchanged at Oct 22) Lumentum (+8.2%), Arm (+6.2%), Coherent (+5.8%), Synopsys (+5.6%) and Bloom Energy (+5.5%) rose most, while Amkor (-6.3%), Advantest (-3.9%), Tokyo Electron (-3.7%), SUMCO (-3.5%) and Nebius (-3.4%) fell most.

items.headline: Meta files for about $35B of stock and preferred; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom signal interest
items.summary: Meta's Oct 26 prospectus filings cover about $22.5B of Class A shares and roughly $12.5B of mandatory-convertible preferred depositary shares to help fund its $135-145B 2026 capex. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom have indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $5B of the common stock, and the filings also mention a possible later at-the-market program of about $60B.

items.headline: SpaceX lines up about $40B of Apollo-managed lease financing for Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs
items.summary: An Apollo-managed vehicle would buy Nvidia AI chips and servers and lease them to SpaceX for about five years, with leases starting in the first half of 2027. SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, calls it the largest committed GPU financing, and expects Q4 capex of $35-40B.

items.headline: China's draft AI export-control list reportedly clears DeepSeek and MiniMax for overseas release
items.summary: Beijing's Oct 16 draft would add 23 AI technologies, including AI chip design and high-speed cluster interconnects, to its restricted or banned export list, with comments open until Nov 15. A state-media-affiliated account says DeepSeek and MiniMax completed registration for open-source and overseas licensing, a claim the outlet had not independently verified.

items.headline: Nvidia unveils Minerva, an AIOps platform for AI data-center uptime and goodput
items.summary: At GTC Berlin, Nvidia introduced Minerva, which combines infrastructure and workload telemetry and uses AI models to flag problems early in AI data centers. It measures output as AI factory yield from GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and tokens produced.
